transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-09 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 55 minutes (recorded)
- Location: Zoom call recorded via Fireflies
- Attendees: Maeve, Arjun, Luis (Redwood); Jordan, Priya, Samir, Taylor (Brightwell)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Maeve opened the kickoff, quick introductions. Discussed staging handoff, connectivity (VPC peering), security checklist (SOC2, KMS), pilot scope (3-week pilot, perf targets), and next steps: run a benchmark, deliver runbook, schedule deep-dive. Customer asked about latency vs cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted, and data residency. Action items assigned.

Topics Identified:
- Staging environment access and network setup
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS)
- Pilot scope and success metrics (latency SLO, token cost)
- Benchmarking plan and runbook
- Rollout timeline and stakeholders

Transcript body:
00:00:05 Maeve (Redwood): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick check, can you all hear me ok?
00:00:09 Jordan (Brightwell): Yep, loud and clear.
00:00:11 Maeve: Great. I'll do a 30 second round of intros — I'm Maeve, CSM. Arjun is our account lead and Luis will own the technical side.
00:00:21 Arjun (Redwood): Morning all, Arjun here.
00:00:23 Luis (Redwood): Luis — hi everyone.
00:00:25 Taylor (Brightwell): Taylor, product. Looking forward.
00:00:27 Priya (Brightwell): Priya, platform.
00:00:29 Samir (Brightwell): Samir, security.
00:00:31 Jordan: Jordan, CTO.

00:01:10 Maeve: Cool, goal for today is to hand off staging access, agree pilot success criteria, and confirm security artifacts you need. We'll also schedule a perf run next week. Any additions?
00:01:21 Jordan: That's right. We also want to make sure this pilot mirrors our production egress and VPC restrictions as close as possible.
00:01:30 Luis: Totally — we built a staging workflow for exactly that. For Redwood Private we can either do VPC peering or use a transit gateway. In staging we usually do peering then mirror routing.
00:01:45 Priya: Peering is preferred. We'll provide CIDR and FIP details, but we need a clear list of ports and protocols.
00:01:53 Luis: Understood. We'll send a network checklist. Expect TCP 443 outbound, and optionally 22 if you want SSH for support; but we can avoid SSH and use vaulted keys.
00:02:05 Samir: On the security front we need to know where logs live, retention, and which team has access. Also KMS — do you integrate with customer-managed keys?
00:02:16 Luis: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private, and for Dedicated we can integrate KMS or HSM depending on your compliance. Logs can be routed to your logging endpoint; default retention is 30 days unless you enable extended retention.
00:02:33 Maeve: I'll attach the SOC 2 and encryption excerpts after the call. Samir, we'll need your checklist items so we can make sure we include artifacts.
00:02:42 Samir: I'll paste our compliance list in the ticket; want to include SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, audit logs, role-based access.
00:02:51 Arjun: Quick note on model hosting options: for the pilot you asked for predictable latency. We recommend starting on Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) for the benchmark because it removes noisy neighbor effects. But if you want a faster time-to-value we can run hosted endpoints first.
00:03:06 Taylor: What's the delta in cost between hosted and dedicated for a pilot?
00:03:10 Arjun: For short pilots hosted is usually cheaper OPEX, but Dedicated gives more consistent p95 latency. I'll send a short cost proforma after.
00:03:20 Jordan: Our main metric is p95 < 220ms for 1k tokens, and we want token costs under $0.002 per token or equivalent — is that realistic?
00:03:32 Luis: 1k tokens is a long sequence. It depends on quantization and batching. With a fp16 or 4-bit quantized variant on Dedicated, p95 around 150-200ms is possible for many models; token cost depends on batching. We'll put together a suggested config.
00:03:49 Priya: For benchmarking we need a few things from you: an initial prompt set, the model/size recommendation, and the harness to replay requests.
00:03:58 Luis: We'll provide a small harness and an example prompt set. We typically include KV cache warmup scenarios since Brightwell will use context window caching.

00:05:30 Arjun: Timeline proposal: today hand off staging, by next Tuesday staging keys + network working, week of 2026-09-20 run benchmark, week after evaluate results and decide on Dedicated commit. Thoughts?
00:05:45 Jordan: That works. We're aiming to have a pilot decision in three weeks.
00:05:51 Maeve: Great — I'll capture that as the target timeline.

00:08:10 Samir: A couple of security questions — is telemetry scrubbed of PII by default? We have customer PII and need strong controls.
00:08:21 Luis: By default we don't persist customer prompt content in logs unless you enable retention. For Private deployments data never leaves your VPC unless you opt in. For hosted we redact or mask by policy; we'll share specifics.
00:08:36 Samir: And audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for admin actions.
00:08:41 Luis: Audit logs are supported; for Private you can ship them to your SIEM. For hosted we can provide export for a retention window.

00:12:00 Taylor: On integration questions: what's the recommended way to do canary rollouts? We might want gradual rollout with automatic fallback.
00:12:09 Maeve: Redwood Console supports rollout policies natively — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model. We'll demo that in a follow-up.
00:12:20 Arjun: Also, if you want automated fallback to a hosted variant for burst, that can be configured in routing policies. Useful if Dedicated hits a capacity limit.
00:12:32 Priya: Ok good. We want to test both canary and fallback behaviors in staging.

00:18:15 Jordan: Regarding data residency — we have EU customers; we need data to stay in eu-west-1. Can you pin region for Dedicated?
00:18:24 Luis: Yes we can pin region. For Private we expect customer-managed infra in the region; for Dedicated we can reserve capacity in eu-west-1. We'll note that in the runbook.

00:22:40 Maeve: Let's talk about success criteria for the pilot. I propose: 1) p95 latency target met for core flows, 2) token cost within 10% of proforma, 3) integration & SSO validated, 4) no security issues from compliance artifact review. Sound reasonable?
00:22:55 Jordan: Yes. Add functional quality checks — model responses passing a set of evaluation prompts with >=95% acceptance by Product.
00:23:04 Taylor: We'll prepare an eval set of 200 prompts and pass/fail criteria.
00:23:08 Maeve: Perfect. We'll include that in the pilot success doc.

00:29:00 Luis: Technical note: for caching, Brightwell's use case — repeated product description lookups — benefits from prefix and KV caching. We'll recommend enabling prefix caching with a TTL of 30 minutes for the staging test to see hit rates.
00:29:12 Priya: Do we need any infra changes to support that?
00:29:16 Luis: No infra changes; caching is runtime-configurable but it does change cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll show expected token savings in the benchmark sheet.

00:36:00 Arjun: Pricing — high level: pilot estimate for 3 weeks of Dedicated usage plus engineering support. I'll follow up with a line-item proforma.
00:36:10 Jordan: Please include both hosted and dedicated scenarios side-by-side. Our finance team will want to see TCO for scaling to 10k requests/day.
00:36:18 Arjun: Will do.

00:42:05 Priya: Quick network gotcha we ran into previously — our egress NAT requires specific FIP allocations. We'll share our NAT table and FIP ranges. Will that be enough?
00:42:13 Luis: That's perfect. We'll validate against our ingress allowlist and confirm any extra endpoints we call out.
00:42:21 Maeve: We'll include a network checklist attachment to the ticket.

00:47:50 Samir: One more: incident response. If there's a compromised key, how fast can you rotate keys and what is the blast radius?
00:48:01 Luis: For Private you own the KMS so rotation is your process. For Dedicated/Hosted we can rotate keys; rotation time depends on session length — we can provide a plan for emergency rotation. We'll document typical RTOs in the runbook.
00:48:14 Samir: Ok please include the RTO and clear owner responsibilities.

00:52:05 Maeve: To recap and close: action items — I'll send the runbook and SOC2 excerpts; Arjun will send pricing proforma; Luis will provision staging key and perf harness; Priya will share VPC/CIDR and NAT details; Samir will send the compliance checklist. We'll aim to have staging validated by 2026-09-14 and run the benchmark week of 2026-09-20.
00:52:26 Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
00:52:30 Maeve: Thanks — we'll follow up in the CRM with tickets and the shared doc links.
00:52:35 Taylor: Appreciate it.

Links referenced: onboarding runbook (will be attached), staging checklist (network.json), SOC2 excerpt PDF, perf_harness repo (link to be shared).

End of transcript.
